claim_results.reason: Within the declared numerical scope, positive-density interface maps preserve lifted half turns, and the right-D/right-N targets are respectively n*pi and (n-1/2)*pi. Constant-density checks, integer/half-integer interface checks, and independent 85-digit transfer calculations on five layered geometries passed. The checked modes had the required interior zero counts; maximum relative frequency discrepancy was 2.608e-15. Successful shorter calls reproduced prefixes exactly. Default calls matched explicit D calls. Tested invalid geometry, insufficient refinement, and unresolved frequency/eigenvalue scales raised exceptions.

Immutable table construction, detached prefixes, geometry/BC binding, zero-based-to-one-based pole conversion, wrong-pole rejection, near-pole rejection, and coverage checks passed the exercised cases. Current main and targeted legacy call sites use consistent shared tables and pole indices. However, the accepted finite-real target domain contains a reproducible denominator-overflow case: full Green evaluation returns an incorrect finite zero instead of rejecting unresolved arithmetic. This violates the requested denominator-resolvability behavior; see F1.

Executed both half-problem CLIs and both rawko CLIs at R=4, sup/inf, N=80, plus all four fixed green-inertia cases. Closed raw Ko agreed with physical-edge FD within 4.376e-10; cross-parity KpOdd agreed with E Ke E from FD within 4.483e-10. Matching-truncation projections used K=diag(1/jumps)J, Kp=diag(eps)Kdiag(eps), and normalized reversal bases. Candidate full-J comparisons differed by at most 3.448e-12. Independently assembling individual spectral summands reproduced raw and conjugated H/E/K sectors within 1.532e-12 across the checked truncations. Legacy c_e/c_o metadata correctly identifies KpEe/KpEo. Visible finite-tail discrepancies, including approximately 0.02473 for one closed-versus-truncated raw Ko comparison, were not treated as identity failures or infinite-dimensional certification.

findings.expected: The independent 90-digit constant-density four-mode sum is approximately 0.0181183475127593823. Either compute the sum with suitable scaling or explicitly reject the unresolved arithmetic.
findings.observed: Returns 0.0 with two overflow warnings, in both ordinary and -O execution. The negative target satisfies the implemented finite-real input domain and is away from every pole.
findings.problem: Spectral differences can overflow before entering the protected arithmetic block. Infinite retained denominators pass the small-denominator test, and division by infinity produces zero, which passes the final finiteness check.
findings.requested_change: Protect spectral subtraction against overflow and reject nonfinite retained denominators, or use scaled arithmetic. Add this case to the rejection/accuracy checks.

limitations: All 15 frozen input hashes matched the manifest and remained unchanged. Execution used isolated copies at /tmp/r12-stateless-review-y_2qj36n/inputs. Recorded project-module origins resolved to those copies; the source project was not modified.

Candidate checks passed 135 cases in ordinary mode and 135 in -O mode. Independent checks recorded 265 passes and the one failure reported above. Commands, timings, outputs, module origins, hashes, and reviewer test sources are retained in the evidence directory.

The debug2/debug3 main routines were not executed within this bounded review; their imports and current table/pole call sites were checked. Historical quadrature routines and scans were not revalidated.
Default-D compatibility was exercised within the supplied snapshot. No historical implementation baseline was supplied for version-to-version comparison.

Floating-point and high-precision numerical checks provide no rigorous interval bounds, universal error guarantee, infinite-dimensional Green-formula proof, global sign theorem, or complete formalization.
